chapter_theme: Two songs at Thiruvotriyur (திருவொற்றியூர், Adhipuri): the poet asks for knowledge before the world mocks him as a maniac of love, and not to be born again in a woman's womb but to reach the Siva-state; the praise names Murugan the guru whom Nataraja praises.

686.reading: The poet, plunged in lovemaking with women of dark hair and carp eyes, their breasts scented with musk and sandal, asks for the grace of knowledge before the world laughs at him in every way as a madman reciting Kama's arts. The praise names Murugan the guru-king whom Nataraja praises and whom Brahma, Vishnu, gods, sages and Siva-yogis extol, the son of Siva who holds the skull, shares his body with a woman and is golden-bodied, at Adhipuri.
686.nuance: The fear named is public mockery (உலகோர்கள் ... நகைகள் கூறி), not Death or hell. நடராஜர் பரவு குருராஜ: Siva the dancer praises Murugan as guru. ஆதிபுரி is Thiruvotriyur.

687.reading: In a dense run of Sanskrit names of the Lord as self-luminous form, cosmic form and true bliss, the poet asks whether, not born again in the womb of women, and gaining the grace of the light of compassion, he will reach the blameless Siva-state and be rid of all troubles. The praise names Murugan with the cock banner, nephew of Vishnu with the discus, Kumara, Guha, Siva-Subrahmanya, death to the demons, the son of the first Siva at Thiruvotriyur by the sea, who dwells in the hearts of the great tapasvins of yoga.
687.nuance: மாதர் வயிறு இடையூறு கருவிற் பிறவாதபடி: release is asked as never again entering a woman's womb. The opening compounds (சொருபப்பிரகாச விசுவரூப ப்ரமாக நிசசுக) read as Sanskrit epithets, but their divisions and the sense of துலியப்பிரகாச are uncertain.

links.note: The Naladiyar says those who take a worthless woman's love as their own will be laughed at by many (பெறுபவே தாமாம் பலரால் நகை). The poet, sunk in love-making, asks for knowledge before the world mocks him every way (உலகோர்கள் ... நகைகள் கூறி) as a madman reciting Kama's arts. Both make public laughter the end of infatuation; the song turns it into the reason to seek knowledge now.

Tirumular says the First removes darkness, carries one past countless births (எண்ணில் பிறவி கடத்தி) and grants grace so that it never leaves. The poet asks that, gaining the grace of the light of compassion (கருணைப்பிரகாச உனது அருளுற்றிட), he not be born again in a woman's womb (கருவிற் பிறவாதபடி) and reach the Siva-state. Both make grace the agent that ends birth.
